2、梳理人形机器人全流程维修闭环:故障接收、问题诊断、备件更换、功能测试、整机校验、问题复盘,优化维修步骤,缩短 MTTR,提升维修效率与一次性修复率。
3、主导机器人翻新、利旧业务规划与落地,制定翻新标准、利旧件筛选规范、拆机复用流程、旧件检测方案,最大化利用可复用零部件,降低售后与生产成本。

5、针对高频故障(线束接触不良、网口异常、通信故障、硬件老化等)输出改善建议,联动维修团队、售后NPI团队、研发团队进行设计收敛。
6、建立维修台账、翻新利旧物料台账,整理故障案例库、维修经验库,完成维修数据统计、成本核算、翻新效率分析,定期输出业务报告。
7、配合项目需求,完成机器人返厂维修、批量翻新、备件管理、客户问题技术支持等工作,推动利旧业务标准化、流程化、可复制。

本岗位为产品服务体系核心岗位,主要负责公司产品可服务性全生命周期管理、服务标准化体系搭建及一线团队技术赋能。统筹新产品服务导入、现场技术支撑、服务质量闭环优化等全维度工作,联动内部项目组与全国一线技术支持团队,平衡产品服务适配性、客户体验与服务效率,推动公司售后服务体系规范化、标准化、本地化迭代升级。
岗位职责
1、产品可服务性全流程管控与资料沉淀:主导产品可服务性(DFS)全周期管理,覆盖服务需求调研提报、设备拆装部署、现场维护调测、故障问题评审复盘、优化方案落地全流程;负责服务侧全套标准化技术资料开发与迭代更新,包含安装部署手册、维修指南、备件BOM清单、拆装机教学视频、FAQ知识库等;牵头新产品上市服务导入工作,提前完成服务资源储备,打通新品上市服务链路,保障新品市场化服务高效、有序落地。
2、数据驱动产品迭代:基于售后端积累的维修数据、故障反馈、客户投诉等,识别产品的系统性的和质量风险,独立或协同质量、研发团队开展失效分析、方案验证及流程优化,向研发团队提出可落地的改进建议并跟进闭环,推动产品迭代完善。
3、服务标准化搭建与一线技术赋能:基于产品服务规范及行业服务标准,编制一线服务标准化培训教材、专项课程课件,常态化组织一线服务人员开展技术培训、实操赋能与技能考核;将产品技术要求、售后服务准则拆解为可落地、可执行的标准化操作流程,监督全国技术支持团队落地执行,统一服务作业标准,保障全国服务质量一致性、专业性。
4、一线疑难支撑与服务质量闭环优化:作为一线服务技术后盾,协助排查解决现场各类复杂疑难故障、技术卡点,搭建轻量化、降本增效的问题分析与处置工具、方法论;常态化收集现场故障案例、客户投诉与优化建议、市场服务痛点,联动研发、项目组开展产品质量整改、性能优化及服务流程迭代,形成“问题收集-分析复盘-优化落地-效果验证”的完整闭环,持续降本增效、提升客户满意度与产品市场口碑。
岗位亮点
1、核心刚需岗位:深度参与产品从上市到运维的全周期服务体系搭建,掌握公司服务业务核心链路,岗位价值高、不可替代性强;
2、能力全面赋能:兼顾技术攻坚、方案设计、体系标准化、团队赋能多维度工作,跳出单一售后执行工作,综合能力成长速度快;
3、发展空间广阔:可深度联动研发、项目、市场多部门,参与产品质量与服务体系迭代,拥有完善的成长路径和晋升通道;

fields.duties:
The Fleet Operations Robot Captain is the mission lead for robot health, uptime, and utilization. This role acts as the primary technical bridge between Research Scientists, Software Developers, Operations and Hardware SMEs to ensure the humanoid fleet remains "mission-ready." The Captain is responsible for leveraging real-time monitoring tools to oversee fleet status, performing high-level technical triage to localize system failures, and manage the experimental pipeline to maximize hardware throughput. This role requires a unique blend of systems engineering knowledge, diagnostic intuition, problem solving ability, and the organizational discipline to manage complex, competing priorities in a fast-paced R&D environment.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Triage & Issue Localization
Act as the first responder for robot hardware and software issues, performing system-level triage to localize failures and determine appropriate escalation paths.
Analyze logs, telemetry, and system behavior to narrow issues to specific subsystems or components.
Create high-quality issue reports and tickets that enable subject-matter experts to root cause problems efficiently.
Identify and escalate fleet-level blockers or safety risks that impact robot availability or operational continuity.
Fleet Monitoring & Status Management
Maintain the real-time health, configuration, and connectivity of all robots in the fleet.
Distinguish between hardware availability and software-induced downtime to ensure accurate reporting and planning.
Ensure fleet status, availability, and constraints are clearly communicated to stakeholders to avoid conflicts or idle time.
Experiment & Queue Management
Own and prioritize the daily experiment and test queue to maximize robot utilization during core operating hours.
Balance risk by sequencing experiments appropriately, enabling progress while minimizing extended downtime.
Provide clear visibility into what is running now, what is next, and expected completion timelines for all active users.
Repair & Operational Coordination
Serve as the primary interface to repair and maintenance teams when hardware intervention is required.
Track repair progress and validate robot readiness before returning systems to active use.
Coordinate software updates and system configuration changes to ensure robots are operating on approved, stable builds.
Execute standardized startup, shutdown, and handoff procedures to ensure continuity across shifts.
Core Competencies
Technical Troubleshooting:
Rapidly localizes faults across complex electromechanical and software boundaries.
Operational Ownership:
Strong sense of accountability for fleet uptime, readiness, and reliability. Makes sound decisions under pressure while balancing risk, safety, and productivity.
Communication:
Translates complex technical issues into clear, actionable information for diverse audiences.
Execution Discipline
: Maintains operational rigor in a fast-moving, high-stakes R&D environment.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Strong understanding of robotics systems, including software stacks, controls, networking, and hardware interfaces.
Proficiency in reading and interpreting Real-Time (RT) code, Linux system logs, and networking telemetry to troubleshoot controls.
Experience with issue tracking, work management systems, such as JIRA, and data-driven monitoring tools/dashboards such as Tableau.
Ability to stay calm and organized while managing multiple high-priority streams of work.
Strong understanding of safety best practices in high-energy or mobile robotics environments.
Typical Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field preferred.
5 years of experience in robotics operations, systems engineering, or a highly technical site reliability role.
Proven track record of troubleshooting complex electromechanical systems.
Experience in a high-intensity R&D environment where hardware availability is a critical path to project success.
The base pay range for this position is between $116,000.00 to $160,000.00 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors, including, but not limited to, internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  This range represents a good-faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off, and an annual bonus structure.  Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.
#LI-CG1

fields.duties:
As the
RMAC Applications Lead
, you will lead the primary engineering team at the Robotic Mobile Application Center (RMAC), responsible for leading the team that drives the transition of the Atlas humanoid robot into production-level automotive manufacturing.
This is a high-impact leadership role that combines the strategic responsibilities of a
Fleet Operations Robot Captain
with the technical oversight of data collection curriculum design and site integration. You will manage a team of Applications Engineers to ensure the RMAC fleet remains "mission-ready" while architecting the playbooks that define how Atlas learns complex sequencing and assembly tasks.
Key Responsibilities
1. Team Leadership & Strategic Coordination
Manage and mentor
a team of Applications/Integration Engineers to ensure day-to-day operations align with Boston Dynamics’ product strategy and automotive industry requirements.
Act as the primary technical bridge
between the Atlas Engineering and Product teams and local Operations/Hardware SMEs.
Collaborate directly with the Atlas product and behavior teams
to implement best practices and provide critical field feedback on system performance and usability.
Coordinate with HMGMA and Glovis stakeholders
on data and workflow integration of Atlas products
2. Data Architecture & Curriculum Design
Lead the process development
for consistent collection of high quality data and creation of test scenarios executed by the onsite robot operations team.
Own the creation of detailed playbooks
for data collection, ensuring that all generated data meets QA standards for the 10,000-hour collection goal.
Define success criteria
and oversee the execution of Operational Level Testing (OLT) and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) for behavior policies.
Playbook Development:
Ensure that playbook creation process and content maintains alignment across Atlas operations within BD and at partner sites
Pilot Coaching & Evaluation:
Provide expert feedback and coaching to Robot Pilots on best techniques; partner with the annotation team to identify and correct poor piloting trends.
3. Fleet Mission Control (Robot Captain)
Serve as the mission lead
for robot health, uptime, and hardware utilization across the RMAC fleet.
Oversee high-level technical triage
, localizing complex system failures across hardware and software boundaries to determine escalation paths.
Prioritize the daily experiment queue
to maximize hardware throughput and balance progress with operational risk.
Coordinate with onsite HW support
and Waltham-based engineering to resolve systemic field issues and track fleet reliability metrics (MTBF, MTBR).
4. Site Integration & Deployment
Develop the processes and practices
required to integrate Atlas into active automotive manufacturing environments.
Oversee site-level solution architecture
, including the management of secure network infrastructure for robust system connectivity.
Facilitate pilot execution
in HMGMA facilities once applications have successfully passed OLT.
Desired Skills & Qualifications
Education:
Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
Experience:
5–7+ years of professional experience in robotics operations, systems engineering, or field application engineering, with at least 2 years in a lead or supervisory capacity.
Technical Proficiency:
Deep understanding of
robotics systems
, including software stacks, controls, and electromechanical hardware interfaces.
Expertise in
Linux (Ubuntu)
, networking telemetry, and reading/interpreting Real-Time (RT) code.
Proficiency in
Python, C++, or scripting
for automating workflows and troubleshooting.
Mastery of
JIRA
for issue tracking and
Tableau
for data-driven monitoring.
Communication:
Exceptional ability to translate high-level R&D concepts into actionable information for executive stakeholders and daily operators.
Travel & Availability
Ability and willingness to travel domestically to other potential Atlas deployment sites or to Boston Dynamics HQ
Ability to support a multi-shift operation (6am–2pm and 2pm–10pm) as needed to ensure fleet continuity.
The pay range for this position is between $177,207.64  to $221,509.55  annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and an annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.

Staff Field Application Engineer
Job Summary:
As a Staff Field Application Engineer (FAE), you will spearhead the delivery of our Enterprise Robotics Integration Program model for Boston Dynamics’ most high-value, strategic accounts. In this pivotal role, you merge deep technical expertise with a business-centric Go-To-Market strategy to design, integrate, and scale robotic solutions across global multi-site enterprises. You are the vital link between high-level governance and on-the-ground execution, ensuring that our robots deliver measurable operational impact.
You will work in synergy with Sales, Customer Success, Global Support & Services, and Product R&D teams, ensuring that the cohesive technical program drives measurable operational impact and accelerated, long-term enterprise adoption. Your expertise is critical in championing long-term product evolution by proactively gathering, systematizing, and conveying field-proven requirements, insights, and customer feedback to internal development teams. You will lead technical projects that enhance program efficiency, standardize playbooks, and drive continuous improvement, ensuring adherence to industry standards, developing program-level SOWs and customer enablement through training and operational support.
Key Responsibilities:
The Strategic FAE serves as the technical lead and orchestrator for the Enterprise Robotics Integration Program model across a customer's fleet. The key responsibilities are:
Program Architecture & Global Strategy:
Lead the creation of complex solution architecture for large-scale, multi-site integrations. Design scalable robotics programs that include infrastructure planning, network integration, and global expansion strategies.
Cross-Functional Orchestration:
Act as the primary technical point of contact for strategic accounts, working in synergy with Sales, Customer Success, Global Support & Services, and Product R&D teams to align technical solutions with measurable business growth.
Governance & Standardization:
Establish and maintain high-quality program standards, including Statements of Work (SOWs) and repeatable integration playbooks, ensuring all activities adhere to industry and regulatory requirements.
Enterprise System Integration:
Act as the technical advisor for robotic data integration and operational workflows into customer enterprise systems (e.g., CMMS, asset management, and data analysis pipelines).
Customer Enablement & Value Measurement:
Deliver advanced training to build internal program ownership within customer teams and implement frameworks to measure the operational value and utilization of the robot fleet.
Product & Engineering Collaboration:
Systematize customer feedback and field data to push critical insights into the internal development cycle, serving as a direct channel to influence the Boston Dynamics product roadmap.
Internal Leadership & Mentorship:
Guide other FAEs and integration teams, identifying patterns in field data to drive long-term optimizations and continuous improvement of the global integration roadmap.
Core Competencies:
Strategic Program Leadership:
Mastery of complex, large-scale robotics integration and enterprise program management. Leads large-scale, multi-site projects, prioritizing technical streams for maximum, scalable operational impact across the full solution lifecycle. Operates effectively and adapts to shifting priorities in global environments.
Synergistic Enterprise Alignment:
Builds and maintains strong, consultative partnerships across business units and stakeholders. Acts as the primary technical contact for strategic accounts, using exceptional communication to align technical execution with the customer's long-term business growth strategy.
System Integration Mastery:
Deep expertise in multi-site, high-complexity product integrations, optimizing performance across hardware, software, and networking systems. Possesses strong analytical skills for diagnosing and resolving highly complex technical issues to ensure maximum operational impact.
Standardization & Mentorship:
Develops and standardizes new integration workflows, repeatable playbooks, and customer enablement strategies to advance enterprise autonomy and fleet performance. Drives continuous excellence through technical mentorship and competence in producing high-quality technical documentation.
Product & Go-To-Market (GTM) Influence:
Systemically synthesizes patterns from field data and customer feedback, directly influencing the strategic direction of the global product roadmap. Familiarity with technical GTM, early product testing, and scaling customer success.
You Must Have:
Education
: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related technical field, or equivalent industry experience.
Experience
: 5+ years of professional experience with a Bachelor’s degree, or 3+ years with a Master’s degree, in fast-paced technology integration, robotics, or complex systems engineering environment.
Strategic Integration Expertise:
Proven track record of overseeing high-complexity technical deployments and managing the intersection of hardware, software, and operational workflows.
Communication & Influence:
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively to engineering teams, operators, and business stakeholders, ensuring alignment on project goals and impact.
We Value:
Operational Adaptability:
Proven comfort in refining and optimizing processes to ensure global scalability and consistent performance across diverse sites.
Technical Versatility:
Ability to leverage CAD for site planning, navigate enterprise networking (VLANs/VPNs) during setup, and utilize Python or C++ APIs to customize robotic solutions and collaborate with technical stakeholders.
Resilience & Autonomy:
Comfort navigating the ambiguity of early-stage product deployments and the ability to build structure where none exists.
Go-To-Market Instinct:
The ability to recognize how a successful technical integration can unlock broader strategic impact and account expansion.
Industrial Domain Expertise:
Familiarity with specialized workflows in sectors like large-scale manufacturing and logistics.
Location & Workplace:
Corporate Headquarters:
This is an in-person role based out of our headquarters in Waltham, MA, offering direct access to our engineering labs and cross-functional teams.
Travel:
Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 50% of the time.
Ability to utilize personal credit cards for travel expenses, with subsequent reimbursement.
Work Authorization:
Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. Boston Dynamics cannot sponsor visas for this role.
The pay range for this position is between
$115,000
to $130,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and a annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.

title: Associate Director of Prototype Fleet & Repair

fields.duties:
Job Summary
The Associate Director, Prototype Fleet & Repair is a senior operational leader responsible for the full lifecycle of the Atlas robot fleet after it leaves the production line, from deployment and health monitoring through field support, repair, and return to service. This role owns two tightly coupled verticals: Fleet Operations, which ensures every deployed robot is available, healthy, correctly configured, and triaged quickly if damaged and/or faulted; and Service & Repair, which drives rapid repair diagnosis, repair execution, and continuous improvement of MTTR and repair quality across all programs.
The ideal candidate is an operator who thinks in systems. Someone who can build and manage high-performing technical teams, establish disciplined processes, drive data-informed improvements, and represent the fleet and repair function at the leadership level. They are comfortable in both a strategic planning meeting and on the floor with a repair technician, and they hold themselves accountable to the same standards they set for their team.
Key Responsibilities
Fleet Operations
Own overall fleet health and availability for all deployed Atlas robots across internal sites and external partner/customer locations.
Establish and continuously improve fleet monitoring, triage, and escalation processes, ensuring every robot issue is captured, routed, and resolved with urgency and accountability.
Build and lead the Internal Application Engineer (IAE) team: Robot Captains and Fleet Operations Technicians, responsible for day-to-day robot health, readiness, and internal customer/partner satisfaction.
Define and track key fleet metrics including Availability, Utilization, MTB Fall, MTB Failure, and fleet-wide uptime, with a standing cadence to report progress and surface risks to leadership.
Own the asset management system and fleet health tracking infrastructure; ensure real-time visibility into robot status, location, configuration, and reservation across all sites.
Partner with Engineering to develop and ultimately manage the FRU (Field Replaceable Unit) strategy, ensuring critical spares are stocked at the right locations to minimize downtime at partner and internal sites.
Drive a Tiered Technical Support model in collaboration with Global Support Services (GSS), ensuring clear escalation paths and ownership for field issues.
Develop & coordinate hardware retrofit campaigns and preventative maintenance programs across the fleet.
Service & Repair
Own end-to-end repair operations for Atlas robots across full-robot, sub-assembly, actuator, and PCBA repair, with a target of <1 hour MTTR for critical repairs.
Lead the Service & Repair team (day and night shift supervisors, R&D repair technicians, PCBA repair technicians) to consistently hit capacity and quality targets.
Develop, maintain, and continuously improve repair work instructions, troubleshooting guides, and diagnostic playbooks to drive speed, consistency, and first-time quality.
Own and improve the repair intake, triage, and return-to-operations workflow, ensuring robots move through the repair process without unnecessary delays or ambiguity.
Partner with Quality & Test Engineering to close the loop on field failures, feeding repair data into root cause analysis, NCR processes, and design/supplier feedback.
Drive Lean improvements in repair layout, tool access, spare parts positioning, and technician workflow to reduce cycle time and eliminate waste.
Support external-facing repair capability including the Service & Repair Trailer for events, POCs, and partner site deployments.
Leadership & Cross-Functional
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing, multi-disciplinary team across fleet ops and repair, setting clear goals, delivering regular feedback, and creating meaningful growth paths.
Partner closely with the TPM function to coordinate fleet priorities, surface dependencies, and align resourcing across competing program needs.
Represent Fleet & Repair in ProtoOps, Atlas and Executive leadership forums, and cross-functional reviews, communicating status, risks, and asks with clarity and credibility.
Collaborate with Engineering on robot reliability trends, field failure data, and design feedback that can prevent future fleet and repair issues upstream.
Develop and manage the Fleet & Repair operating budget, headcount plan, and facilities requirements to support scaling Atlas programs and beyond.
Core Competencies:
Operational rigor
Builds systems, not heroics. Establishes clear processes, metrics, and accountability structures so the team performs consistently, not just when the leader is in the room.
People leadership
Invests in team development, navigates performance with directness and care, and creates an environment where technical talent can do their best work.
Customer focus
Treats internal customers and external partners as the ultimate judge of fleet quality. Proactively identifies what “healthy fleet” means to each customer and builds to that bar.
Data-driven execution
Makes decisions grounded in fleet metrics, repair data, and trend analysis, not gut feel. Establishes the right KPIs, tracks them consistently, and uses them to drive improvement.
Adaptability
Thrives in the tension between scaling a new program and maintaining quality. Finds paths forward when the plan changes, and keeps the team grounded and productive through ambiguity.
Cross-functional influence
Builds trust and credibility with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and external partners. Advocates effectively for fleet and repair needs without creating friction.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:
Deep understanding of field operations, fleet management, and repair execution for complex electromechanical systems: robotics, aerospace, or equivalent preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and scale technical teams (engineers and technicians) across multiple functions in a dynamic environment.
Strong grasp of key fleet operations metrics (OEE, Availability, Utilization, MTTR, MTB Fall/Failure) and experience driving measurable improvement against them.
Experience developing and maintaining repair processes, work instructions, and diagnostic playbooks for complex hardware systems.
Familiarity with FRU strategy, spare parts planning, and min/max inventory management for field-deployed hardware.
Proficiency with fleet tracking and asset management systems; comfort evaluating and implementing new tools as the program scales.
Skilled at root cause analysis, Lean/continuous improvement methods, and driving cross-functional corrective action.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, able to represent the team clearly in leadership settings and at the floor level.
Ability to operate across strategic planning and day-to-day execution without losing effectiveness at either end.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, or Industrial Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline. Advanced degree or MBA a plus.
10+ years of experience in field operations, service & repair, fleet management, or a closely related operational role in a hardware product environment.
5+ years of people management experience, including managing managers or senior supervisors.
Prior experience in a robotics, aerospace, automotive, or high-complexity electromechanical product environment strongly preferred.
Track record of building operational infrastructure, processes, metrics, systems, in a scaling or early-stage program.
Experience managing repair or service operations across multiple sites or locations preferred.
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.

Job Summary
The Associate Director, Prototype Fleet & Repair is a senior operational leader responsible for the full lifecycle of the Atlas robot fleet after it leaves the production line, from deployment and health monitoring through field support, repair, and return to service. This role owns two tightly coupled verticals: Fleet Operations, which ensures every deployed robot is available, healthy, correctly configured, and triaged quickly if damaged and/or faulted; and Service & Repair, which drives rapid repair diagnosis, repair execution, and continuous improvement of MTTR and repair quality across all programs.
The ideal candidate is an operator who thinks in systems. Someone who can build and manage high-performing technical teams, establish disciplined processes, drive data-informed improvements, and represent the fleet and repair function at the leadership level. They are comfortable in both a strategic planning meeting and on the floor with a repair technician, and they hold themselves accountable to the same standards they set for their team.
Key Responsibilities
Fleet Operations
Own overall fleet health and availability for all deployed Atlas robots across internal sites and external partner/customer locations.
Establish and continuously improve fleet monitoring, triage, and escalation processes, ensuring every robot issue is captured, routed, and resolved with urgency and accountability.
Build and lead the Internal Application Engineer (IAE) team: Robot Captains and Fleet Operations Technicians, responsible for day-to-day robot health, readiness, and internal customer/partner satisfaction.
Define and track key fleet metrics including Availability, Utilization, MTB Fall, MTB Failure, and fleet-wide uptime, with a standing cadence to report progress and surface risks to leadership.
Own the asset management system and fleet health tracking infrastructure; ensure real-time visibility into robot status, location, configuration, and reservation across all sites.
Partner with Engineering to develop and ultimately manage the FRU (Field Replaceable Unit) strategy, ensuring critical spares are stocked at the right locations to minimize downtime at partner and internal sites.
Drive a Tiered Technical Support model in collaboration with Global Support Services (GSS), ensuring clear escalation paths and ownership for field issues.
Develop & coordinate hardware retrofit campaigns and preventative maintenance programs across the fleet.
Service & Repair
Own end-to-end repair operations for Atlas robots across full-robot, sub-assembly, actuator, and PCBA repair, with a target of <1 hour MTTR for critical repairs.
Lead the Service & Repair team (day and night shift supervisors, R&D repair technicians, PCBA repair technicians) to consistently hit capacity and quality targets.
Develop, maintain, and continuously improve repair work instructions, troubleshooting guides, and diagnostic playbooks to drive speed, consistency, and first-time quality.
Own and improve the repair intake, triage, and return-to-operations workflow, ensuring robots move through the repair process without unnecessary delays or ambiguity.
Partner with Quality & Test Engineering to close the loop on field failures, feeding repair data into root cause analysis, NCR processes, and design/supplier feedback.
Drive Lean improvements in repair layout, tool access, spare parts positioning, and technician workflow to reduce cycle time and eliminate waste.
Support external-facing repair capability including the Service & Repair Trailer for events, POCs, and partner site deployments.

Build, develop, and retain a high-performing, multi-disciplinary team across fleet ops and repair, setting clear goals, delivering regular feedback, and creating meaningful growth paths.
Partner closely with the TPM function to coordinate fleet priorities, surface dependencies, and align resourcing across competing program needs.
Represent Fleet & Repair in ProtoOps, Atlas and Executive leadership forums, and cross-functional reviews, communicating status, risks, and asks with clarity and credibility.
Collaborate with Engineering on robot reliability trends, field failure data, and design feedback that can prevent future fleet and repair issues upstream.

Invests in team development, navigates performance with directness and care, and creates an environment where technical talent can do their best work.
Customer focus
Treats internal customers and external partners as the ultimate judge of fleet quality. Proactively identifies what “healthy fleet” means to each customer and builds to that bar.

Makes decisions grounded in fleet metrics, repair data, and trend analysis, not gut feel. Establishes the right KPIs, tracks them consistently, and uses them to drive improvement.

Thrives in the tension between scaling a new program and maintaining quality. Finds paths forward when the plan changes, and keeps the team grounded and productive through ambiguity.

Builds trust and credibility with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and external partners. Advocates effectively for fleet and repair needs without creating friction.

Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, able to represent the team clearly in leadership settings and at the floor level.
Ability to operate across strategic planning and day-to-day execution without losing effectiveness at either end.

10+ years of experience in field operations, service & repair, fleet management, or a closely related operational role in a hardware product environment.
5+ years of people management experience, including managing managers or senior supervisors.
Prior experience in a robotics, aerospace, automotive, or high-complexity electromechanical product environment strongly preferred.
Track record of building operational infrastructure, processes, metrics, systems, in a scaling or early-stage program.

Field Repair Technicians
who can work as key members of our multidisciplinary team to troubleshoot, test, and repair complex robotic systems for our on-site Atlas fleet at the Robotic Mobile Application Center (RMAC). This role is a unique blend of mechanical assembly and sophisticated electronic troubleshooting. You will be responsible for maintaining our humanoid platform, ensuring that one of the world's most advanced humanoid robots maintains peak performance during rigorous testing cycles.
Key Responsibilities
Mechanical Systems:
Perform complex repairs and preventive maintenance on high-performance humanoid robots.
Precision Tooling:
Utilize hand tools and torque wrenches to meet exacting tolerances; Atlas requires extreme precision to maintain balance and structural integrity.
Diagnostics:
Use laptop computers, multimeters and oscilloscopes to troubleshoot power distribution systems, sensor arrays, and communication bus issues.
Hardware-Software Integration:
Work within a Linux environment to run system checks, utilizing BASH scripts and Python routines to verify hardware health after repairs.
Collaboration:
Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams across engineering, software, and operations to resolve issues and maintain maximum robot uptime.

Maintain accurate records of parts inventory, tracking consumption and availability to ensure operational readiness for all repair tasks.

Mechanical Expertise:
Extensive experience with mechanical assembly and teardowns.
Electrical Fundamentals:
Proficiency in reading schematics and using a multimeter for continuity and voltage testing.
Technical Literacy:
Ability to interpret complex engineering drawings and BOMs (Bill of Materials).
Physically capable of lifting 50 pounds unassisted.

Software:
Comfort with Linux (Ubuntu/Debian) command-line operations.
Experience in Automotive, Aviation or specialty repair and maintenance.

Ability to read/write basic BASH and Python for automation of repetitive test sequences.
Specialized Systems:
Experience with high-voltage battery systems and complex electro-mechanical systems.

2nd shift role with the ability to cover 1st shift as needed

The Mission
Boston Dynamics is rapidly scaling the Atlas humanoid fleet from prototype development to large-scale deployment. As a Fleet Operations Application Engineer, you will serve as the technical quarterback for fleet health, reliability, and operational execution.
You are the first line of technical response when a robot experiences an issue. Your responsibility is to quickly determine whether the problem originates in software, controls, hardware, networking, infrastructure, or operator workflow, then coordinate the right technical experts to restore fleet availability.
This role sits at the intersection of Prototype Operations, Controls Engineering, Software Engineering, Hardware Engineering, and Research. Success requires broad technical knowledge, exceptional troubleshooting ability, strong operational leadership, and excellent communication.
What You'll Do
Fleet Technical Operations
Serve as the first technical point of contact for robot issues across the fleet.
Continuously monitor fleet health, availability, telemetry, and mission readiness.
Own operational awareness across all active robots while communicating fleet status and needs to engineering and leadership.
Balance robot availability, experiment schedules, repairs, and software releases to maximize fleet utilization.
Technical Triage
Perform rapid system-level troubleshooting across controls, software, hardware, networking, sensors, power systems, and infrastructure.
Analyze logs, telemetry, system behavior, and robot performance to isolate failures.
Determine root-cause hypotheses and drive the appropriate escalation path.
Distinguish between software defects, controls issues, hardware failures, configuration errors, and operational problems.
Create high-quality engineering tickets containing sufficient technical detail for efficient resolution.
Incident Leadership
Lead technical incident response meetings during fleet-impacting events.
Coordinate Software, Controls, Electrical, Mechanical, Manufacturing, and Repair teams during active troubleshooting.
Drive clear ownership, priorities, action items, and follow-up.
Communicate technical status to engineers, management, and stakeholders throughout an incident.
Fleet Reliability
Identify recurring failure modes across the fleet.
Partner with engineering teams to improve diagnostics, health monitoring, automation, and tooling.
Recommend process improvements that reduce downtime and improve robot reliability.
Develop troubleshooting playbooks and operational procedures for repeatable issues.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Act as the technical bridge between Fleet Operations and Engineering.
Support software deployments, hardware upgrades, and configuration management.
Coordinate repairs and validate robot readiness before returning systems to service.
Ensure lessons learned from fleet operations directly influence future robot designs.
Who You Are
A systems thinker who enjoys solving complex technical problems spanning multiple engineering disciplines.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity while making sound technical decisions under pressure.
Able to quickly narrow problems without immediately jumping to conclusions.
An exceptional communicator who can translate technical information for engineers, technicians, and leadership.
Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple high-priority issues simultaneously.
Naturally collaborative and comfortable leading cross-functional discussions without direct authority.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
5+ years supporting complex electromechanical products or technical operations.
Experience managing or supporting an operational fleet of robots, autonomous vehicles, industrial equipment, aircraft, ships, manufacturing systems, or similarly complex assets.
Experience troubleshooting systems that integrate software, controls, networking, sensors, and hardware.
Experience leading technical incident response or operational reviews.
Strong understanding of Linux, networking fundamentals, and system diagnostics.
Experience using issue tracking and operational management tools such as Jira, ServiceNow, or similar platforms.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with humanoid robots, autonomous systems, industrial robotics, or advanced automation.
Familiarity with controls systems, motion control, embedded software, or real-time systems.
Experience reading robot logs and telemetry to diagnose failures.
Experience with Python or scripting for data analysis or automation.
Understanding of version control, software deployment, and configuration management.
Experience developing operational procedures, playbooks, or troubleshooting documentation.
The pay range for this position is between $154,000 to $200,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and a annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.

Lead test infrastructure projects (planning, budgeting, vendor coordination, installation, validation).
Develop and revise lab and testbed layouts.
Coordinate electrical, networking, and mechanical integration.
Submit and manage purchase requisitions.
Technical Operations
Perform and oversee software and hardware testing.
Lead troubleshooting across mechanical, electrical, and software systems.
Maintain lab power, video, and safety infrastructure.
Interpret schematics and technical documentation.
Lab Management
Oversee daily lab operations to ensure a safe, organized, and fully functional testing environment.
Manage lab assets, tooling, and equipment.
Ensure readiness of lab spaces, including safety systems, power distribution, and environmental controls.
Systems & Process Improvement
Improve testing workflows and infrastructure reliability.
Develop documentation standards and operational best practices.
Maintain detailed project and operational documentation in assorted systems.

Serve as a liaison between operations and engineering teams.
Coordinate directly with vendors, contractors, and facilities personnel.
Support high-visibility demonstrations and executive-level visits.

Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related technical field or equivalent hands-on experience.

Strong knowledge of electronics, electrical systems, and mechanics.
Proficiency with Linux or command-line systems.
Advanced troubleshooting and analytical skills.
Strong communication and organizational skills.
